Toggle Between the Current and Alternate File Card
Toggle Between the Current and Alternate File Card
Description: Switches to the alternate file — the buffer edited before this one — and pressing it again switches back. With a count, {N}<C-^> edits buffer N instead.
Toggle Between the Current and Alternate File Card

You press Ctrl and 6. No Shift. ^ sits on the 6 key, and Ctrl with that key produces the character vim calls CTRL-^ — the name describes the character, not the keys, which is why it looks harder to type than it is. On some non-US layouts it is produced another way (:help CTRL-^).
Toggle Between the Current and Alternate File Card

The case it wins is two files edited in alternation, because it does not care where either one sits in the buffer list — unlike <S-h> / <S-l> in LazyVim/Keyshort/Buffer, which step through that list in order.
The alternate file is held in the # register, which is why :e # does the same thing in a longer form. The registers are set out on nvim/Q/What does " mean in nvim?.
Identical in vim and nvim, and LazyVim does not rebind it.

Toggle Folding Itself On and Off Card
Toggle Folding Itself On and Off Card

Description: Flips the foldenable option. Distinct from zR — zR opens folds while leaving folding active, zi suspends folding entirely and remembers which folds were closed when it is switched back on.
Toggle Folding Itself On and Off Card

In my LazyVim config folding is foldmethod=indent with foldlevel=99, so files open fully expanded and folds follow indentation rather than syntax. That makes zM immediately useful on Logseq pages and Python, where indentation already carries the structure.
No nvim-ufo is installed, so zR and zM are the built-in commands rather than ufo's remapped versions, and there is no virtual text showing folded line counts.

Description: Applies the filetype's indent rules to the motion's range, fixing structure without reformatting content. Different from <leader>cf, which runs a real formatter.

Description: Jumps to the first line, then re-indents from there to the last. Reads as three ordinary commands composed: gg move, = operator, G motion.

= uses equalprg or the filetype indent plugin, so on a file with no indent support it falls back to lisp-style indenting and can do more harm than good. Reach for LazyVim/Keyshort/Code Action <leader>cf when a real formatter is configured.

Join the Next Line onto This One Card
Join the Next Line onto This One Card
Description: Pulls the following line up, collapsing the leading whitespace and inserting a single space at the seam. Takes a count — 3J joins three lines — and works over a visual selection.
Join the Next Line onto This One Card
Join Without Inserting a Space Card
Join Without Inserting a Space Card
Description: Same join, but keeps the text exactly as it is: no space inserted and leading whitespace preserved. The one to use when the line break is inside a string or a path.
Join Without Inserting a Space Card
The everyday use is unwrapping a hard-wrapped paragraph; gqip re-wraps it afterwards to textwidth.
Not to be confused with <S-l>, which is a buffer jump in my LazyVim config — see LazyVim/Keyshort/Buffer.
Jump Back and Forward Through the Jump List Card
Jump Back and Forward Through the Jump List Card
Description: Steps through vim/jump/list, the record of every position jumped away from — across files, not just within a buffer. The browser back/forward button of Vim.
Jump Back and Forward Through the Jump List Card
The Mnemonic: O for older, I for the opposite (and <C-i> is the same byte as <Tab>, which is why <Tab> sometimes appears to jump forward).
Jump Back and Forward Through the Jump List Card
Description: Prints the jump list with position 0 as the most recent entry.
This is what makes gd safe to press freely: jump to a definition, read it, <C-o> back to where the question started (see LazyVim/Keyshort/LSP/Navigation).
Only jumps are recorded — searches, G, gg, marks, and tag jumps. Plain j / k movement is not, so the list stays coarse enough to be useful.
The same two keys navigate help tags, which is the context they are documented in on vim/Keyshort/Help/Tag/Browse Back and Forward. <leader>sj in LazyVim opens a picker over the list.
Shortcut: m followed by a letter, e.g. ma
Description: Drops a named mark at the cursor. Lowercase letters are local to the buffer; uppercase letters are global and carry a file with them, so mA jumps back across files.
Shortcut: `a exact position, 'a start of line
Description: Backtick returns to the exact line and column of mark a; the apostrophe returns to the first non-blank character of that line.
Jump Back to Where I Just Was Card
Jump Back to Where I Just Was Card
Description: Returns to the position before the last jump, using the automatic ' mark. The one mark worth knowing even without setting any by hand.
Jump Back to Where I Just Was Card
Description: Clears marks by name or range — :delmarks ax removes just a and x, :delmarks! clears all lowercase marks for the buffer while leaving A-Z and 0-9 intact.

Marks are only worth setting if they can be found again; <leader>sm in LazyVim opens a picker over every set mark with its file and line, which removes the need to remember letters (see LazyVim/Keyshort/Search).
Distinct from the jump list, which records where I have been automatically rather than where I chose to bookmark — see vim/Keyshort/Jump/Back and Forward.
